strategic_themes.title: Lift qualified audit opinion (Ernst & Young LLP)
strategic_themes.rationale: External auditor issued a qualified opinion on 2024/25 statements. Direct: PSAA scale fee normalisation. Indirect: lifting governance flag reduces borrowing-cost premium. Manual read of audit report needed to itemise qualification reason — once known, target single-cycle remediation.

strategic_themes.title: HNSG Reform Plan submission — secures £144.9M DSG write-off (90% of £161.0M)
strategic_themes.rationale: DSG cumulative high-needs deficit £161.0M. Under the new High Needs Stability Grant (HNSG) announced 9 Feb 2026, government will write off 90% (~£144.9M) of every council's DSG deficit at 31 March 2026 via Section 31 grant paid Autumn 2026 — CONDITIONAL on the council submitting an approved Local SEND Reform Plan to DfE by 19 June 2026. The £16.1M residual remains on council books. Safety Valve programme closed 1 April 2026 and is folded into HNSG. Statutory override extended to 31 March 2028; gov has committed to absorb all DSG deficits from 1 April 2028 onwards. The savings range below covers (a) plan-submission cost avoidance + (b) residual 10% in-year demand management.
strategic_themes.delivery_horizon: 19 June 2026 plan submission deadline; Autumn 2026 grant payment
strategic_themes.implementation_complexity: medium — plan submission is procedural, not discretionary
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Director of Children's Services + S151 Officer + Cabinet Lead SEND
evidence: GOV.UK Explanatory note on DSG deficits (9 Feb 2026)

strategic_themes.title: Highways term-maintenance contract benchmarking (£1000M)
strategic_themes.rationale: Highways term-maintenance contract: Milestone Infrastructure (M Group Services). . Open-book pricing review, JCT-style PPM benchmarking, social-value measurement and rate-card comparison vs Crown Commercial Service framework rates standard. 3-7% saving on labour/materials/overhead lines typical from open-book in early-contract period.

strategic_themes.title: LGR / One Suffolk LGR plan: £39.4M annual saving from year 5
strategic_themes.rationale: Council has published LGR business case targeting £39.4M/yr by year 5 / £78.2M cumulative. Components: 16 locality teams, property rationalisation, digital innovation, planning consolidation, highways restructuring. Delivery risk is the standard LGR pattern: stand-up costs front-loaded, savings back-loaded; year-1-2 net cost typical.

strategic_themes.title: Treasury management + borrowing cost optimisation (CFR proxy £880M)
strategic_themes.rationale: Annual revenue £1100M implies indicative CFR c. £880M. Standard levers: internal borrowing from earmarked reserves, PWLB Certainty Rate trade, MMF counterparty restructuring, LGPS Property Investment Pool inclusion. 10-30bp saving on external debt typical from a fresh review.

strategic_themes.title: LGPS employer contribution opportunity (2025 triennial valuation cycle)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative pay bill £440M × c. 22% employer contribution rate = £97M annual employer contribution. Most LGPS funds materially over-funded post-2022 (returns 2022-25 averaged 7-10% pa vs 3-4% discount-rate assumption). 2025 triennial valuation typically yields 2-4pp employer-rate reduction over 2026-2029. Confirm with administering authority + actuary.

strategic_themes.title: Capital programme phasing + Treasury impact review (£292.2M)
strategic_themes.rationale: Capital programme £292.2M. Standard pattern in s.114-watch councils: TM impact per scheme, defer / cancel non-mandatory + non-invest-to-save schemes, prioritise borrowing capacity. Capital costs c. 4-6% annually (MRP + interest). Deferring 10-20% of programme by 12 months saves 0.5-1.2% of total programme value as MRP+interest avoidance — recurring once delivered.

strategic_themes.title: Fees, charges + traded-services income optimisation (£110M base)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative fees & charges + traded-services income c. 10% of revenue = £110M. Standard levers: annual CPI uplift discipline, full-cost-recovery audit on discretionary services (parking, planning, licensing, sports, adult learning, property hire), commercial pricing on traded services. LGA experience: 5-15% income uplift sustainable over 2-3 years.

strategic_themes.title: Insurance retention + premium review (£1.1M premium estimate)
strategic_themes.rationale: Indicative insurance premium £1.1M (10bp of revenue). Standard 3-5 yr renewal cycle. Levers: tender via IPG / RM Partners (10-25% premium reduction typical), retention review (increase excess + build risk-fund reserve). London-borough cohort average 12% premium reduction at last tender.

strategic_themes.title: Contracts Finder portfolio review (84 notices; 2 contracts at £10M+ ceiling)
strategic_themes.rationale: Contracts Finder data: 84 notices (72 awarded, £8M aggregate ADVERTISED CEILING value, 0% SME). IMPORTANT: advertised contract value is a CEILING set to avoid retender risk under PCR 2015 Reg.72 / Procurement Act 2023 s.31 — actual spend through the awardee is typically 30-70% of ceiling, with some off-contract ledger spend permitted within the 50%/50% modification limits. 2 contracts at £10M+ ceiling totalling £50M (ceiling, NOT spend) — top 3: Suffolk Energy Action Framework - AWARD (ceiling £25M); Suffolk Energy Action Framework (ceiling £25M). SME-awarded share 0% is below the Procurement Reform 2023 / PPN 03/24 ambition (33% SME share by value). Standard procurement-data savings levers (% of ACTUAL ledger spend, not ceiling): (a) modification-history scrutiny under PCR 2015 Reg.72, (b) Procurement Act 2023 s.31 contract change notice review, (c) re-tender benchmark vs CCS framework rates on next renewal. 2-8% on actual spend through major contracts is a defensible upper bound.
strategic_themes.decision_owner: Head of Procurement + Cabinet Member + Section 151 Officer

strategic_themes.title: Companies House compliance follow-up (£7M flagged — 1 overdue, 1 dissolved, 0 insolvency-history)
strategic_themes.rationale: Companies House lookup on top-50 suppliers identified £7M of spend with statutory-compliance flags: £4M to suppliers with overdue accounts (1), £4M to dissolved-status companies (1), £0M to companies with insolvency history (0). NOTE: Some matches are CH fuzzy-search false positives (e.g. school, government-body name collisions) and need human verification. After verification, real flags = (a) credit-risk review on overdue accounts, (b) contract-cleanup on dissolved entities (records still on ledger but supplier extinct — risk of duplicate-payment leakage), (c) PCR 2015 Reg.57 discretionary exclusion review on insolvency-history suppliers in active contracts.

strategic_themes.title: Rebuild general reserves to ≥4 months (Low → Adequate)
strategic_themes.rationale: Reserves at 3.3 months (Low per CIPFA Resilience benchmark). Direction: improving. A 4-month minimum is the CIPFA / S151 prudence floor; below this triggers external auditor VFM concern and elevates s.114 risk.

strategic_themes.title: Audit + recover £140M in flagged duplicate-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE forensic flagged £140M across 25,865 groups of likely duplicates. Industry recovery norm 5-15% via duplicate-detection software (AP Forensics, FISCAL, Oracle Concur). Lloyds Bank Commercial Card analysis typical for spot-check sample of 100 highest-confidence matches.

strategic_themes.title: Investigate £222M in flagged split-payment patterns
strategic_themes.rationale: DOGE flagged £222M across 0 split-payment instances. Split payments often indicate (a) below-procurement-threshold ledger fragmentation circumventing PCR 2015 Reg.4 contract-value-aggregation rule; or (b) legitimate sub-line invoice splits. Sample audit + reclassify; misuse triggers Reg. 99 challenge exposure.
